column2: Zelophehad's genealogy reaches Joseph through Manasseh, and all five daughters appear in the same order as 26:37.
The daughters stand before Moses, Eleazar, rulers and the whole assembly at the tent entrance. All four audiences remain.
Their father died for his own sin, not in Korah's uprising, and had no sons. The distinction does not identify his particular sin.
The petition seeks preservation of the father's name and a possession among his brothers. Both purposes remain.
Moses brings their legal case before the Lord instead of issuing his own ruling.
Divine speech introduces the judgment.
The daughters are declared right and emphatically granted the father's allotment among his brothers. Gift and transfer both remain.
A deceased man without a son transmits inheritance to his daughter, generalizing the case.
If there is no daughter, the selected recipient is his brother in the singular.
If there are no brothers, the selected recipient is the father's brother in the singular.
Without paternal brothers, the nearest tribal relative inherits. The rule is identified as a judicial ordinance through Moses.
The selected parenthesis identifies the farther-side mountain as Nebo and explicitly names Canaan as the promised possession.
Moses sees the land and is gathered like Aaron at Hor. The selected Hor location remains.
The charge concerns both leaders' transgression and failure to sanctify God at the water. The selected expanded explanation and Kadesh identification remain.
Moses addresses the Lord before requesting succession.
The Lord is God of spirits and all flesh, asked to appoint a man over the assembly.
Four leading/moving clauses culminate in the sheep-without-shepherd image. No repeated movement is omitted.
Joshua has spirit within himself; Moses lays hands, plural, on him. The source does not require an added theological identification of that spirit.
Presentation before Eleazar, instructions to Joshua and instructions concerning him before the assembly all remain.
Propose some of your glory for the partitive construction, supplying natural English for the inherited put of your glory. The transfer's purpose remains Israel's obedience.
Joshua stands before Eleazar, and plural they ask him for the judgment of the manifestations. Going and coming follow his word.
column3: The technical manifestations term and pronoun reference need specialist review; no unexamined Hebrew term is substituted.

column2: Moses obeys by presenting Joshua before priest and whole assembly.
Moses lays both hands and presents Joshua as commanded. The selected commissioning verb remains provisionally presented.
Divine speech opens the scheduled offerings.
Three gift/offering expressions and their first-person possessives remain, together with careful presentation at God's feasts.
column3: Donations for the second gift noun is provisional and needs a further literary-register review.

column2: Two unblemished year-old lambs are required daily for continual whole burning.
One lamb is morning and the second toward evening; both times remain.
The accompanying flour is one tenth oiphi with one quarter hin oil.
The continual offering is connected to Sinai and sweet savour. Instituted is the provisional contextual rendering of its coming-to-be there.
Each lamb's drink is one quarter hin of strong drink, poured in the holy place. Strong drink is not silently changed to wine here.
The evening lamb repeats with its sacrifice and drink offering, preserving the daily parallel.
Sabbath adds two unblemished year-old lambs, two tenths flour with oil and drink offering.
The Sabbath offering is additional to the continual offering and its drink, not a replacement.
New-moon animals are two calves, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Flour measures are three tenths per calf and two per ram, both with oil.
Each lamb receives one tenth flour with oil, followed by the sacrifice/savour/offering description.
Wine is half a hin per calf, one third per ram and one quarter per lamb, repeated monthly through the year.
One sin goat is added to the continual offering and its drink offering.
Passover falls on the fourteenth day of month one.
The fifteenth begins the festival and seven days of unleavened eating.
The first day is a holy assembly with no laborious work, preserving the qualified work prohibition.
The festival's whole burnt animals are two calves, one ram and seven year-old lambs, all unblemished.
Three tenths flour per calf and two per ram accompany them with oil.
Each of the seven lambs receives one tenth; the distributive repetition is rendered each.
One male goat for sin makes atonement for the people.
These are additional to the morning continual offering; its repeated continual description remains.
The prescribed gifts recur daily for seven days, with drink offering alongside the continual offering.
The seventh day repeats holy assembly and no laborious work.
New produce and the new offering at weeks occasion holy assembly and the work restriction.
The weeks offering again has two calves, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
The weeks flour measures remain three tenths per calf and two per ram.
Each of the seven weeks lambs receives one tenth flour.
One sin goat provides atonement in the weeks list.
The offering is additional to the continual one, with sacrifice to Me, unblemished qualification and drink offerings all retained.
The first day of month seven is a holy assembly and signalling day, with no laborious work. No unspecified instrument is inserted here.
The first-day animals are one calf, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Flour with oil is three tenths for the calf and two for the ram.
Each of the seven lambs receives one tenth flour.
One sin goat is included for atonement.
New-moon and continual offerings are additional. Propose singular continual whole burnt offering to match the selected noun, retaining the plural accompanying sacrifices and drinks.
The tenth day requires holy assembly and affliction of souls, with all work prohibited rather than only laborious work.
Its unblemished animals are one calf, one ram and seven year-old lambs.
The tenth-day flour measures are three tenths per calf and two per ram.
Each of the seven lambs receives one tenth flour.
One sin goat is additional to the atonement sin offering and daily offering, with prescribed sacrifice, drink and savour. The fuller selected ending remains.
Month seven's fifteenth day begins a seven-day festival with holy assembly and no laborious work.
Day one explicitly has thirteen calves, two rams and fourteen year-old lambs, unblemished.
Three tenths per each of thirteen calves and two per each of two rams are retained.
Each of fourteen lambs receives one tenth flour.
Day one's sin goat and continual offering with associated sacrifices and drinks remain additional.
Day two reduces calves to twelve while retaining two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Day two's sacrifice and drink follow each animal count and prescription; the selected singular collective terms remain.
Day two repeats one sin goat and the additional daily offering with its accompaniments.
Day three has eleven calves, two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Day three retains the singular collective sacrifice/drink wording and number-based prescription.
Day three repeats the sin goat and daily offering clause in full.
Day four has ten calves, two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Day four uses plural sacrifices and drinks, distributed according to animal numbers and prescription.
Day four's additional sin goat and continual-offering clause remain.
Day five has nine calves, two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Day five's plural accompanying offerings follow animal counts and prescription.
Day five repeats one sin goat and the daily-offering provisions.
Day six has eight calves, two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
Day six's accompanying sacrifices and drinks follow the counted animals.
Day six repeats the sin goat and additional daily offering in full.
Day seven has seven calves, two rams and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs, completing the descending calf sequence.
Day seven preserves both according-to-number and according-to-prescription clauses.
Day seven retains one sin goat and the continual offering with its accompaniments.
The eighth day is the selected closing festival with no laborious work.
The eighth-day animals are one calf, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs, distinct from the prior seven days.
The singular calf and ram and plural lambs receive accompanying offerings by their numbers and prescription.
The eighth day also includes one sin goat besides the continual offering and accompaniments.
Festival obligations are distinguished from vows, freewill, whole burnt, sacrifice, drink and deliverance offerings; all six categories remain.
